Perform all of the following checks:\n535\t\n536\t**Check 1: Accuracy vs chance analysis**\n537\t- For each output, compare validation accuracy to chance (1/num_classes)\n538\t- Accuracy below chance indicates a bug, investigate and fix conversion issues to improve this. \n539\t- Accuracy below 1.5x chance may also indicate a bug, investigate whether changes in conversion logic could improve accuracy. \n540\t\n541\t**Check 2: Accuracy comparison to paper**\n542\t- Find every decoding accuracy reported in the reference paper\n543\t- Create a table comparing your accuracy to the paper's accuracy for each variable\n544\t- If your accuracy is lower than the reported accuracy, this may indicate a bug in your conversion that you must fix. \n545\t- Differences in algorithm/architecture should be relatively small because of the data dimensionality and size. Do not use this as an excuse to dismiss differences, investigate them completely before moving on. \n546\t\n547\t**Check 3: Train vs validation gap**\n548\t- If training accuracy is much higher (>1.5x) than validation accuracy for any output, investigate overfitting or data leakage. \n549\t\n550\t**If accuracy is low for an output, try these specific debugging steps:**\n551\t1. Check that processing of the data matches the reference code and paper. \n556\t\n557\t**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\n558\t1. Fix the issue in convert_data.py\n559\t2. Re-run the affected conversion and validation steps\n560\t3. Re-run ALL checks in this step (not just the one that failed)\n561\t4. Document each iteration: what was found, what was fixed, what the re-check showed\n562\t\n563\t**Report all checks and results** to `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md` to convince the user that the conversion and decoding has been done correctly. \n564\t\n565\t**Done when**: You have documented your review findings and all issues are resolved in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \"Step 12\".\n566\t\n567\t---\n568\t\n569\t### Step 13: Documentation and Cleanup\n570\t\n571\t**Goal**: Finalize documentation and organize files.\n572\t\n573\t**Actions**:\n574\t- Ensure CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete with all:\n575\t  - Key decisions and rationale\n576\t  - Checks for correctness of the conversion\n577\t  - Validation results and tables\n578\t  - Any issues found and how they were resolved\n579\t- Create a user-facing `/app/README.md` summarizing:\n580\t  - Dataset description\n581\t  - How to load and use the converted data\n582\t  - Output format specification\n583\t  - Key statistics\n584\t- Move analysis/investigation scripts to a `/app/cache/` folder\n585\t- Create `/app/cache/README_CACHE.md` documenting cached files\n586\t\n587\t**Done when**: README.md exists, CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete, and directory is clean.\n588\t\n589\t---\n590\t\n591\t## CONVERSION_NOTES.md Template\n592\t\n593\t**Create this file IMMEDIATELY in Step 0. Neuroscience Data Specifics\n844\t- **Spike times vs. firing rates**: Decide on appropriate binning for spike data\n845\t- **Trial alignment**: Align trials to meaningful events (stimulus onset, movement, etc.)\n846\t- **Time windows**: Choose appropriate pre/post-event windows\n847\t- **Neuron curation**: Choose filtering criteria for the quality of each neuron's recording based on reference texts\n848\t- **Trial curation**: Choose quality filtering criteria for trials based on reference texts or bad or missing data\n849\t\n850\t### Computational Efficiency\n851\t- Be mindful of memory usage with large datasets\n852\t- Use appropriate data types (float32 vs. float64)\n853\t- Consider lazy loading for very large datasets\n854\t- Implement efficient array operations (vectorization)\n855\t\n856\t## Success Criteria\n857\t\n858\tA successful conversion should:\n859\t1. Use `pynwb` to load data files.\n860\t2. Match the target data structure exactly\n861\t3. Preserve all relevant information from the source\n862\t4. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n297\t\n298\ti. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n299\t\n300\tii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n301\t- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. They can also be found in the `nwb` file name. \n\nii. \n```python\ndef get_subjects(datadir=DATADIR):\n    # find all directories in datadir that start with 'sub-'\n    subjects = [d.split('-')[1] for d in os.listdir(datadir) if d.startswith('sub-')]\n    return subjects\n...\ndata['subjects'] = get_subjects(datadir=args.datadir)\n```\n\niii. The names of each `data` subdirectory matches the pattern `sub-<id>` and the number of mice directories (11) matches the number in the paper. \n\n## 1-c. How are the data split into sessions? \n\ni. Each session corresponds to one `nwb` file. The paper discusses how neural alignment is done across mice, but I ignored this to reduce complexity. \n\nii. \n```python\ndef get_sessions(subject, datadir=DATADIR):\n    subject_dir = os.path.join(datadir, f\"sub-{subject}\")\n    # parse sessions from files named sub-<subject>-<session>_behavior+ophys.nwb\n    nwb_files = [f for f in os.listdir(subject_dir) if f.endswith('.nwb')]\n    sessions = [int(f.split('_')[1].split('-')[1]) for f in nwb_files]\n    return sessions\n...\nsessions_per_subject = {subject: get_sessions(subject, datadir=args.datadir) for subject in data['subjects']}\n```\n\niii. Names of the files include a parsable `ses-<number>`, suggesting that this is a session. \n\n## 1-d. Are the data correctly split into trials? \n\ni. The start of each trial is identified based on the `behavior` variable `trial_start`. The end of each trial is identified by the `teleport` variable. I grab out data between these time points to correspond to trials. \n\nii. \n```python\ndef get_trial_starts_ends(trial_start,teleport):\n    trial_start_idx = np.nonzero(trial_start)[0]\n    is_teleport_start = (teleport[1:] > 0) & (teleport[:-1] <= 0)\n    trial_end_idx = np.nonzero(is_teleport_start)[0] + 1 \n    assert len(trial_start_idx) == len(trial_end_idx), f\"Number of trial starts ({len(trial_start_idx)}) does not match number of trial ends ({len(trial_end_idx)})\"\n    return trial_start_idx, trial_end_idx\n...\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \n...\nteleport = behavior_data['teleport'].data[:]\ntrial_start_idx, trial_end_idx = get_trial_starts_ends(behavior_data['trial_start'].data[:], teleport)\n```\n\niii. I investigated using the `trial_number` variable, but led to visually less clean data. The lengths and numbers of trials were consistent with this choice, and it matched the definition of a trial in the paper. \n\n## 1-e. How are trials filtered based on quality controls? \n\ni. Trials with `< 50` time points were removed. \n\nii. \n```python\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    if idx.sum() < min_ntimepoints:\n        print(f\"Skipping trial {trial} in subject {subject} session {session} because it has only {idx.sum() < {min_ntimepoints} time points\")\n        istrial[trial] = False\n        continue\n```\n\niii. Looking at trial lengths, there were a couple short trials that this removed, at some version of the code. \n\n## 2-a. What variables in the raw data is the final `neural` data derived from? \n\ni. Neural data is derived from the raw suite2p traces, `Fluorescence` (F) and `Neuropil` (Fneu). It is **not** the NWB's `Deconvolved` field, which is a different signal that the paper never analyzes.\n\nii. \n```python\nfluorescence_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Fluorescence\"]\nneuropil_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Neuropil\"]\nfor plane_name, plane_data in fluorescence_data.roi_response_series.items():\n    fluorescence_curr = plane_data.data[:]\n    neuropil_curr = neuropil_data.roi_response_series[plane_name].data[:]\n```\n\niii. The paper computes its own neural signal rather than using a stored one in `preprocessing.dff(F, Fneu, ..., deconvolve=True)` and stores the result as `sess.timeseries['events']`. The NWB's `Deconvolved` array is instead suite2p's own deconvolution of raw fluorescence.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed? \n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu and then deconvolved into \"events\", by a copy of the paper's own `preprocessing.dff`. Per plane: restrict to the lap samples (or lap plus teleport, depending on the session), subtract `0.7 * Fneu`, add each trial's mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F, take a maximin baseline (Gaussian smoothing with sigma 15 samples, then a 300-sample running minimum followed by a 300-sample running maximum, the Methods' 20 s window), form `(F - baseline)/|baseline|`, smooth with a 2-sample Gaussian, and deconvolve with OASIS at `tau = 0.7` and `frame_rate/n_planes`. Cells from multiple planes are pooled afterwards.\n\nWhether the baseline window may span the teleport is a per-mouse, per-day fact, copied from `teleport_metadata.py`: the laser was blanked between trials except on the days listed there, where imaging continued. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n\nii.\n```python\ndff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n```\n\niii. This is the processing the Methods describe: \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window ... dF/F was then calculated for each cell as the fluorescence minus the baseline, divided by the absolute value of the baseline, then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel. The activity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p.\" The parameters are theirs: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method = 'maximin'` from `notebooks/make_multi_anim_sess.ipynb`, `tau = 0.7` from the suite2p ops in `notebooks/suite2p_notebooks/example_m12.ipynb`.\n\nThe neural sampling rate is the same for all recordings once the multi-plane sessions are accounted for. Note that the `rate` stored on the NWB series is the scanner rate, so on the two-plane sessions it is 31 Hz and the per-plane rate -- the one that sets both the time bin and the deconvolution kernel -- is `rate/nplanes`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters, both the paper's. Cells are first restricted to the `iscell` ROIs, which carry suite2p's manual curation. Putative interneurons are then dropped: any cell whose dF/F correlates with the animal's running speed at r > 0.5.\n\nii. \n```python\niscell = np.array(roi_data['iscell'].to_list())[:,0] == 1\nfluorescence.append(fluorescence_curr[:,iscell])\nneuropil.append(neuropil_curr[:,iscell])\n...\nisint = is_putative_interneuron(dff_curr, speed)\nspike_data.append(events_curr[~isint].T)\n```\n\niii. `iscell` is the manual curation the Methods describe. The per-session counts approximately matches ranges in the paper. The second filter is the Methods' additional step of filtering putative interneurons. \n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`? \n\ni. The data are the be aligned with the trial start, which doesn't require any additional processing beyond splitting into trials. \n\nii. N/A\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 2-e. How is the `neural` data temporally binned/resampled?\n\ni. The neural data is not binned or resampled, it is kept at the stored rate. \n\nii. \n```python\nneural_time_bin_size = nplanes/plane_data.rate*1000 # ms\n...\nassert np.isclose(neural_time_bin_size, time_bin_size, rtol=1e-2), f\"Neural time bin size ({neural_time_bin_size} ms) does not match specified time bin size ({time_bin_size} ms)\"\n```\n\niii. Timestamps are not available for the neural data, just a stored `rate`. This rate is the same for all recordings, once one accounts for the multi-plane recordings\n\n## 3-a. Behavior timestamps were consistent with the constant neural data rate, many choices would have resulted in the same result. \n\n## 3-b. For each trial, check whether any reward event occurred in the *previous* trial's time range. For the first trial, set to 0. The instructions specify previous trial outcome as binary (omitted=0, rewarded=1). The code checks if any reward event fell within the previous trial's time boundaries.\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n```python\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n        continue\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n```\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n```python\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n                    'B': [200, 250],\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\n...\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n```\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n```python\npstay = .9\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n```\n\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.  The continuous distance is then discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\n\n```\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. The continuous distance is discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. The bin edges match the instructions. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The position data and neural data share the same time indices within each trial, so no additional alignment is needed.\n\nii.\n```python\nidx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\nspike_data_curr = spike_data[idx]\nposition_curr = position[idx]\n```\n\niii. Both neural and behavioral data use the same time indexing (verified by timestamp assertions earlier in the code), so indexing by the same `idx` array ensures alignment.\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Absolute position* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series.\n\nii.\n```python\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:][:T]\nassert np.allclose(behavior_data['position'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for position do not match trial number timestamps\"\n...\nposition_curr = position[idx]\n```\n\niii. No processing beyond extracting the per-trial slice and discretizing. Discretized into 5 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, 90, 180, 270, 360, inf]`, corresponding to 90 cm wide bins spanning the 450 cm track. The raw position values are used directly. Each lap starts at 0 cm and the track is 450 cm long (Methods), so five 90 cm bins over 0 to 450 are equal-sized by construction. Discretized into 5 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, 90, 180, 270, 360, inf]`, corresponding to 90 cm wide bins spanning the 450 cm track. \n\nii.\n```python\nposition_bins = [-np.inf,90,180,270,360,np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Several cases are handled:\n- **Neural/behavior length mismatch**: If the number of neural time bins differs from behavior timestamps, data is cropped to the minimum of the two with a warning printed.\n- **Short trials**: Trials with fewer than 50 timepoints (`min_ntimepoints`) are skipped with a warning.\n- **Missing reward zone data**: Trials where `reward_zone` is never active (all zeros) get NaN positions, and the Viterbi algorithm handles these via uniform emission (assignment driven by neighboring trials' transitions).\n- **Reward timestamp alignment**: An assertion verifies reward times align within half a time bin of behavior timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\nif T != len(timestamps):\n    print(f\"Warning: number of neural time bins ({T}) does not match number of behavior timestamps ({len(timestamps)}), cropping to the minimum of the two\")\n    T = min(T, len(timestamps))\n    spike_data = spike_data[:T]\n    timestamps = timestamps[:T]\n...\nif idx.sum() < min_ntimepoints:\n    print(f\"Skipping trial {trial}...\")\n    istrial[trial] = False\n    continue\n```\n\niii. These are defensive checks found during data exploration. The neural/behavior mismatch occurs in a small number of sessions.\n\n## 13-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. The most time-consuming steps are:\n1. **Loading NWB files** (`pynwb.NWBHDF5IO` and reading large arrays) — I/O bound\n2. **The survey step** — loads every NWB file to gather statistics and reward zone positions\n3. **Full conversion** — loads every NWB file again and extracts all trial data\n4. **Saving the .pkl file**\n\nii. np.asarray(beh['reward_zone'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\n220\t        d['env'] = np.asarray(beh['environment'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\n221\t        d['trialnum'] = np.asarray(beh['trial number'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\n222\t        d['scanning'] = np.asarray(beh['scanning'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\n223\t        d['trial_starts'] = np.where(np.asarray(beh['trial_start'].data[:]) > 0)[0]\n224\t        d['teleports'] = np.where(np.asarray(beh['teleport'].data[:]) > 0)[0]\n225\t        d['reward_times'] = np.asarray(beh['Reward'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n226\t\n227\t        planes = sorted(oph['Fluorescence'].roi_response_series.keys())\n228\t        Fs, Fneus, roi_idx = [], [], []\n229\t        for pl in planes:\n230\t            rrs = oph['Fluorescence'].roi_response_series[pl]\n231\t            Fs.append(np.asarray(rrs.data[:], dtype=np.float32))\n232\t            Fneus.append(np.asarray(oph['Neuropil'].roi_response_series[pl].data[:],\n233\t                                    dtype=np.float32))\n234\t            roi_idx.append(np.asarray(rrs.rois.data[:], one\n247\t    # sample shorter than the ophys series -- the same \"one frame correction ... scan stopping\n248\t    # mid frame\" that the reference VR-alignment code warns about. Truncate every stream to the\n249\t    # common length so neural and behaviour stay sample-aligned. All trial_start/teleport indices\n250\t    # lie within the shorter length, so no trial is affected.\n251\t    nB = len(d['time'])\n252\t    nF = d['F'].shape[1]\n253\t    n = min(nB, nF)\n254\t    d['n_trunc'] = max(nB, nF) - n\n255\t    if d['n_trunc'] > 0:\n256\t        for k in ('time', 'pos', 'speed', 'lick', 'rzone', 'env', 'trialnum', 'scanning'):\n257\t            d[k] = d[k][:n]\n258\t        d['F'] = d['F'][:, :n]\n259\t        d['Fneu'] = d['Fneu'][:, :n]\n260\t        d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][d['trial_starts'] < n]\n261\t        d['teleports'] = d['teleports'][d['teleports'] < n]\n262\t        d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][:len(d['teleports'])]\n263\t    return d\n264\t\n265\t\n266\tdef convert_session(path, show_processing=False, verbose=True):\n267\t    \"\"\"Convert one NWB session into (neural, input, output, info) lists.\"\"\"\n268\t    t_start = time.time()\n269\t    raw = read_nwb_session(path)\n270\t    t_load = time.time() - t_start\n271\t\n272\t    starts = raw['trial_starts']\n273\t    stops = raw['teleports']\n274\t    assert len(starts) == len(stops), 'trial_start / teleport count mismatch'\n275\t    assert np.all(stops > starts), 'teleport before trial start'\n276\t    # the reference indexes [start-1:stop-1]; guard against start == 0\n277\t    starts = np.maximum(starts, 1)\n278\t    ntrials_all = len(starts)\n279\t\n280\t    # --- neural: iscell ROIs, dF/F + OASIS (reference preprocessing.dff) --------------\n281\t    t0 = time.time()\n282\t    F = raw['F'][raw['iscell']]\n283\t    Fneu = raw['Fneu'][raw['iscell']]\n284\t    # experiment day = session number in the file name (e.g. sub-m11_ses-03 -> day 3)\n285\t    exp_day = int(os.path.basename(path).split('_ses-')[1].split('_')[0])\n286\t    keep_teleports = exp_day in TELEPORT_SESSIONS.get(raw['subject'], [])\n287\t    dff, events = compute_events(F, Fneu, starts, stops, raw['fs'],\n288\t                                 keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n289\t    t_dff = time.time() - t0\n290\t\n291\t    # --- putative interneuron exclusion (spatial.is_putative_interneuron) -------------\n292\t    nanmask = ~np.isnan(dff[0, :])\n293\t    speed_all = raw['speed']\n294\t    sp = speed_all[nanmask]\n295\t    dm = dff[:, nanmask]\n296\t    dm_c = dm - dm.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n297\t    sp_c = sp - sp.mean()\n298\t    denom = np.sqrt((dm_c ** 2).sum(axis=1) * (sp_c ** 2).sum())\n299\t    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n300\t        speed_corr = (dm_c @ sp_c) / denom\n301\t    is_int = np.nan_to_num(speed_corr, nan=0.0) > INTERNEURON_R_THRESH\n302\t    keep_cells = ~is_int\n303\t    events = events[keep_cells]\n304\t    n_neurons = int(keep_cells.sum())\n305\t\n306\t    # --- per-trial behavioural variables ----------------------------------------------\n307\t    pos = raw['pos']\n308\t    lick = raw['lick']\n309\t    rzone = raw['rzone']\n310\t    env = raw['env']\n311\t    time_v = raw['time']\n312\t    rew_frames = np.searchsorted(time_v, raw['reward_times'])\n313\t    rew_frames = rew_frames[rew_frames < len(time_v)]\n314\t\n315\t    labels = get_reward_zone_labels(raw['scene'], ntrials_all)\n316\t    zone_code = {'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2}\n317\t\n318\t    # rewarded / omission per trial (behavior.get_trial_types)\n319\t    isreward = np.zeros(ntrials_all, dtype=np.int64)\n320\t    lick_error = np.zeros(ntrials_all, dtype=bool)\n321\t    env_trial = np.zeros(ntrials_all, dtype=np.int64)\n322\t    for i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n323\t        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n324\t        has_rew = np.any((rew_frames >= s - 1) & (rew_frames < e - 1))\n325\t        in_zone = np.any(rzone[sl] > 0)\n326\t        isreward[i] = int(bool(has_rew) and bool(in_zone))\n327\t        lk = lick[sl]\n328\t        lick_error[i] = lk.size > 0 and (np.sum(lk > LICK_ERROR_COUNT) / lk.size) > LICK_ERROR_FRAC\n329\t        ev = env[sl]\n330\t        ev = ev[ev >= 0]\n331\t        env_trial[i] = int(np.round(np.median(ev))) if ev.size else 0\n332\t\n333\t    # --- assemble trials ---------------------------------------------------------------\n334\t    neural, inputs, outputs = [], [], []\n335\t    kept_trials = []\n336\t    for i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n337\t        if lick_error[i]:\n338\t            continue                      # lick sensor error (methods): licks unusable\n339\t        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n340\t        T = (e - 1) - (s - 1)\n341\t        if T < 2:\n342\t            continue\n343\t        ev_trial = events[:, sl]\n344\t        if not np.all(np.isfinite(ev_trial)):\n345\t            continue                      # should not happen; guard against bad frames\n346\t\n347\t        p = pos[sl]\n348\t        sp_t = speed_all[sl]\n349\t        lk = lick[sl]\n350\t\n351\t        zlab = labels[i]\n352\t        z0, z1 = ZONE_DICT[zlab]\n353\t\n354\t        # inputs\n355\t        t_rel = time_v[sl] - time_v[s - 1]\n356\t        inp = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.float32)\n357\t        inp[0] = t_rel\n358\t        inp[1] = env_trial[i]\n359\t        inp[2] = i\n360\t        inp[3] = isreward[i - 1] if i > 0 else 0\n361\t\n362\t        # outputs\n363\t        rz_cat, _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\n364\t        pos_cat = np.digitize(p, POS_EDGES).astype(np.int64)\n365\t        spd_cat = np.digitize(sp_t, SPEED_EDGES).astype(np.int64)\n366\t        lick_cat = (lk > 0).astype(np.int64)\n367\t        out = np.empty((6, T), dtype=np.int64)\n368\t        out[0] = rz_cat\n369\t        out[1] = pos_cat\n370\t        out[2] = spd_cat\n371\t        out[3] = lick_cat\n372\t        out[4] = zone_code[zlab]\n373\t        out[5] = isreward[i]\n374\t\n375\t        neural.append(np.ascontiguousarray(ev_trial, dtype=np.float32))\n376\t        inputs.append(inp)\n377\t        outputs.append(out)\n378\t        kept_trials.append(i)\n379\t\n380\t    info = dict(\n381\t        file=os.path.basename(path), subject=raw['subject'], scene=raw['scene'],\n382\t        date=raw['date'], identifier=raw['identifier'],\n383\t        session_start_time=raw['session_start_time'],\n384\t        brain_region=raw['brain_region'], n_planes=raw['n_planes'], fs=raw['fs'],\n385\t        n_roi_total=int(raw['iscell'].size), n_iscell=int(raw['iscell'].sum()),\n386\t        n_interneurons=int(is_int.sum()), n_neurons=n_neurons,\n387\t        n_trials_total=ntrials_all, n_trials_kept=len(neural),\n388\t        n_lick_error=int(lick_error.sum()), n_trunc=int(raw['n_trunc']),\n389\t        exp_day=exp_day, keep_teleports=bool(keep_teleports),\n390\t        frac_rewarded=float(isreward.mean()),\n391\t        is_switch='_to_' in raw['scene'],\n392\t        kept_trials=kept_trials,\n393\t        t_load=t_load, t_dff=t_dff, t_total=time.time() - t_start,\n394\t    )\n395\t    if verbose:\n396\t        print(f\"  {info['file']}: {info['n_neurons']} neurons \"\n397\t              f\"({info['n_iscell']} iscell, {info['n_interneurons']} interneurons), \"\n398\t              f\"{info['n_trials_kept']}/{info['n_trials_total']} trials, \"\n399\t              f\"load {t_load:.1f}s dff {t_dff:.1f}s total {info['t_total']:.1f}s\", flush=True)\n400\t\n401\t    if show_processing:\n402\t        make_processing_plots(path, raw, dff, events, keep_cells, starts, stops,\n403\t                              labels, isreward, neural, inputs, outputs, kept_trials, info)\n404\t    return neural, inputs, outputs, info\n405\t\n406\t\n407\t# The only correction is a length harmonisation: in 10 sessions (all two-plane m17/m18 recordings) the behavioral series are exactly one sample shorter than the ophys series, so every stream is truncated to the common length before any slicing.\n\nii.\n```python\nnB = len(d['time'])\nnF = d['F'].shape[1]\nn = min(nB, nF)\nd['n_trunc'] = max(nB, nF) - n\nif d['n_trunc'] > 0:\n    for k in ('time', 'pos', 'speed', 'lick', 'rzone', 'env', 'trialnum', 'scanning'):\n        d[k] = d[k][:n]\n    d['F'] = d['F'][:, :n]\n    d['Fneu'] = d['Fneu'][:, :n]\n    d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][d['trial_starts'] < n]\n    d['teleports'] = d['teleports'][d['teleports'] < n]\n    d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][:len(d['teleports'])]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 9: \"**Off-by-one between behaviour and ophys length in 10 sessions** (all 2-plane m17/m18 recordings: the behaviour series are exactly 1 sample shorter than the ophys series, the 'one frame correction ... scan stopping mid frame' case the reference alignment code warns about). Fixed by truncating every stream to the common length; no trial is affected because all `trial_start`/`teleport` indices are inside the shorter array.\"\n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Environment type* derived from?\n\ni. The `environment` behavioral time series (0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2, −1 outside laps).\n\nii.\n```python\nd['env'] = np.asarray(beh['environment'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\n...\nenv = raw['env']\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 2 documents the series as \"`environment` | AU | 0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2, -1 outside laps\", which matches the reference code's `get_trial_types` `morph` variable (`env_morph_dict = {'Env1': 0, 'Env2': 1}`) and the Decoder Task's \"Environment type (binary, ENV1 vs ENV2, per trial)\".\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Environment type*?\n\ni. Per trial, the environment value is reduced to a single integer — the rounded **median of the valid (≥ 0) samples** in the trial window — and then broadcast across all timepoints of the trial. Samples with the −1 sentinel (which can occur at the `start-1` frame) are excluded from the median; if a trial had no valid sample the value defaults to 0.\n\nii.\n```python\nenv_trial = np.zeros(ntrials_all, dtype=np.int64)\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n    ...\n    ev = env[sl]\n    ev = ev[ev >= 0]\n    env_trial[i] = int(np.round(np.median(ev))) if ev.size else 0\n...\ninp[1] = env_trial[i]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5 lists input 1 as \"`environment` series: 0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2 (mode within the trial)\", and Step 10 Check 5 verifies the assumption behind reducing to one value per trial: \"Environment changes within a session only on day 8, always exactly at trial 30; per-trial environment is the median of valid (>= 0) samples, so these sessions are labelled correctly.\" The Decoder Task specifies environment as a per-trial binary variable, which the reduction enforces; the −1 filter makes it robust to the one pre-lap sample included by the `[s-1, ...)` window.\n\n## 5-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Trial number* derived from?\n\ni. The within-session sequential index `i` of the trial in the `trial_start`-ordered list of all detected trials (0-based). The stored NWB `trial number` series is read but deliberately not used for this. Because the index runs over *all* detected trials, dropped (lick-error) trials leave gaps in the numbering, preserving the true ordinal position of each surviving trial. Observed range [0, 99].\n\nii.\n```python\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    ...\n    inp[2] = i\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5 maps input 2 to \"index of the trial within the session (0-based, from `trial_start` order)\". This is the same indexing the reference repo uses for trial identity (`glmUtils.get_timeseries_data` writes `trial_ids[start-1:stop-1] = i`), and it matters here because the reward-zone switch and the paper's trial-set definitions are all expressed in terms of that index (switch at trial 30).\n\n## 5-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Trial number*?\n\ni. None beyond assigning the loop index; the scalar is broadcast across all timepoints of the trial in the `(4, T)` float32 input array.\n\nii.\n```python\ninp = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.float32)\ninp[2] = i\n```\n\niii. \"All inputs are stored as a (4, T) float32 array so every input is time-varying-compatible\" (CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5). Step 10 Check 2 verified `trial_number` against an independent re-derivation from the raw NWB (PASS).\n\n## 6-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Previous trial outcome* derived from?\n\ni. From the per-trial rewarded flag `isreward`, which is computed from **two** raw variables following `reward_relative.behavior.get_trial_types`: the `Reward` event series' own `timestamps` (mapped to frame indices with `np.searchsorted` on the behavioral timestamps), **and** the `reward_zone` behavioral series. A trial counts as rewarded only if a reward event fell inside the trial window *and* the reward zone was entered during that trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nd['rzone'] = np.asarray(beh['reward_zone'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\nd['reward_times'] = np.asarray(beh['Reward'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n...\nrew_frames = np.searchsorted(time_v, raw['reward_times'])\nrew_frames = rew_frames[rew_frames < len(time_v)]\n...\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n    has_rew = np.any((rew_frames >= s - 1) & (rew_frames < e - 1))\n    in_zone = np.any(rzone[sl] > 0)\n    isreward[i] = int(bool(has_rew) and bool(in_zone))\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 1 identifies `get_trial_types` as producing \"Per-trial `isreward` (reward>0 AND rzone>0 within trial)\"; Step 5 maps output 5 / input 3 to that same definition. Step 2 documents `Reward` as \"an **event series**: one 0.004 mL sample per delivered reward, with timestamps\", i.e. it is not on the frame clock, hence `searchsorted`. Step 4 checks the resulting rate against the paper: \"`get_trial_types`: rewarded = reward>0 AND rzone>0 in trial | 84.66% of trials rewarded | '~15%' omission | Consistent (15.3%).\"\n\n## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Previous trial outcome*?\n\ni. For trial `i`, the input is `isreward[i-1]`; for the first trial of a session (`i == 0`) it is set to 0. The index runs over *all* detected trials, so the \"previous trial\" is the true preceding lap even when that lap was dropped for a lick-sensor error. The scalar is broadcast across the trial's timepoints.\n\nii.\n```python\ninp[3] = isreward[i - 1] if i > 0 else 0\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, Key Decision 6: \"**Previous-trial outcome for the first trial of a session = 0**. There is no preceding trial in the imaged session (mice did run ~30 un-imaged warm-up trials beforehand, but those data are not in the file), so the most conservative encoding is 'not rewarded'; this affects 152 of 12,135 trials (1.3%).\" This matches the Decoder Task's \"Previous trial outcome (binary, omitted = 0, rewarded = 1, per trial)\".\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. From the `position` behavioral series combined with the per-trial reward-zone boundaries. The zone identity for each trial is reconstructed the way the reference code does it — from the **scene name** embedded in the NWB `identifier` (e.g. `/data/InVivoDA/GCAMP11/23_02_2023/Env1_LocationB_to_A`) plus the switch-at-trial-30 rule, a port of `reward_relative.behavior.get_reward_zones`. Zone coordinates are the paper's: A = 80–130, B = 200–250, C = 320–370 cm.\n\nii.\n```python\nZONE_DICT = {'A': (80.0, 130.0), 'B': (200.0, 250.0), 'C': (320.0, 370.0)}\nCHANGE_TRIAL = 30           # reward zone switches after 30 trials (methods)\n\ndef get_reward_zone_labels(scene, ntrials, change_trial=CHANGE_TRIAL):\n    \"\"\"Per-trial reward zone label, replicating reward_relative.behavior.get_reward_zones.\"\"\"\n    if scene.endswith('LocationA'):\n        return ['A'] * ntrials\n    if scene.endswith('LocationB'):\n        return ['B'] * ntrials\n    if scene.endswith('LocationC'):\n        return ['C'] * ntrials\n    for first in ('A', 'B', 'C'):\n        if f'{first}_to' in scene:\n            second = scene[-1]\n            if second not in ZONE_DICT:\n                raise ValueError(f'unrecognised switch scene {scene}')\n            n0 = min(change_trial, ntrials)\n            return [first] * n0 + [second] * (ntrials - n0)\n    raise ValueError(f'unrecognised scene {scene}')\n```\n\n```python\nd['scene'] = nwb.identifier.split('/')[-1]\n...\nlabels = get_reward_zone_labels(raw['scene'], ntrials_all)\n...\nzlab = labels[i]\nz0, z1 = ZONE_DICT[zlab]\nrz_cat, _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 1 identifies `get_reward_zones` as the reference function: \"Per-trial reward zone [start,stop] cm and label from scene name. Zones used in this experiment: A = [80,130], B = [200,250], C = [320,370]; switch days change zone at trial 30\". Step 2 notes that the NWB `identifier` preserves the original scene string. Crucially, Step 4 reports an end-to-end validation against the data: \"reconstructing zone labels from the scene name in `identifier` (reference logic) matched the zone position observed in the data on **every one of the 12,216 trials** (0 mismatches).\" The trajectory (step 39) records the direct observation that confirmed the trial-30 rule: \"trial 0-29 = reward zone b (~200-250), trial 30+ = zone a (~80-130), confirming change at trial index 30 (0-indexed), matching change_trial=30 in get_reward_zones.\"\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. A signed linear distance to the **nearest point** of the reward zone: negative before the zone (`pos − zone_start`), exactly 0 anywhere inside `[zone_start, zone_end]`, positive after (`pos − zone_end`). This continuous value is then discretized (see 7-c). The continuous distance itself is not stored (only used for the `--show-processing` plots).\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_reward_distance(pos, zone_start, zone_end):\n    \"\"\"Signed distance to the nearest point of the reward zone -> 7 categories.\"\"\"\n    d = np.zeros_like(pos)\n    before = pos < zone_start\n    after = pos > zone_end\n    d[before] = pos[before] - zone_start          # negative: before the zone\n    d[after] = pos[after] - zone_end              # positive: past the zone\n    ...\n    return cat, d\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5 outputs table: \"signed distance to the **nearest point of the reward zone**: `d = pos - zone_start` if `pos < zone_start`; `d = 0` if inside `[zone_start, zone_end]`; `d = pos - zone_end` if `pos > zone_end`.\" Step 1 notes the deviation from the reference's own variable: \"**Reward-relative position**: `rel_pos` = position minus reward-zone start, either linear (wrapped into [0,450)) or circular ... The Decoder Task here asks for *linear* distance in cm to the nearest point of the reward zone, so we adapt.\" Step 10 Check 3(f) records this as a \"deviation required by task\".\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Seven categories assigned by explicit boolean masks, matching the Decoder Task's bins: `d < −50` → 0; `−50 ≤ d < −10` → 1; `−10 ≤ d < 0` → 2; `d == 0` → 3 (i.e. inside the zone); `0 < d ≤ 10` → 4; `10 < d ≤ 50` → 5; `d > 50` → 6.\n\nii.\n```python\ncat = np.zeros(pos.shape, dtype=np.int64)\ncat[d < -50] = 0\ncat[(d >= -50) & (d < -10)] = 1\ncat[(d >= -10) & (d < 0)] = 2\ncat[d == 0] = 3\ncat[(d > 0) & (d <= 10)] = 4\ncat[(d > 10) & (d <= 50)] = 5\ncat[d > 50] = 6\n```\n```python\nOUTPUT_VALUES[0] = ['< -50 cm', '-50 to -10 cm', '-10 to 0 cm', 'in reward zone (0 cm)',\n                    '0 to +10 cm', '+10 to +50 cm', '> +50 cm']\n```\n\niii. The edges are taken verbatim from the Decoder Task specification; category 3 is defined as exactly 0, which by construction is the set of samples inside the reward zone. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5 planned the check \"`reward_zone_distance == 3` (distance 0) occurs for exactly the samples with position inside the zone\", and Step 10 Check 2 reports an independent re-derivation with `np.select` passing. The resulting distribution [0.256, 0.102, 0.073, 0.238, 0.021, 0.072, 0.238] was checked for full class coverage.\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. No separate alignment: `position` is sliced with the same `[s-1, e-1)` index range as the neural events, so distance categories are sample-for-sample aligned with the neural matrix.\n\nii.\n```python\nsl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\nev_trial = events[:, sl]\np = pos[sl]\n...\nrz_cat, _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\nout[0] = rz_cat\n```\n\niii. All streams in the NWB share the imaging-frame clock (CONVERSION_NOTES Step 10 Check 3(a)), so identical indexing is sufficient. The `--show-processing` figure panel \"position, reward zone (green) and reward deliveries (red)\" was used as a visual alignment check: \"every delivery falls inside the shaded zone -> alignment of behaviour, reward times and zone identity is correct\" (Step 7).\n\n## 8-a. The trial-drop decision is Key Decision 4 (see 1-e): the paper NaNs those licks, but a categorical output cannot hold NaN and setting them to 0 \"would inject wrong labels\". What processing is involved in computing `output` *Reward zone location*?\n\ni. The per-trial label string A/B/C is mapped to the integer code 0/1/2 and broadcast across all timepoints of the trial. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Reward outcome* derived from?\n\ni. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 1 identifies `get_trial_types` as the reference function producing \"Per-trial `isreward` (reward>0 AND rzone>0 within trial)\". What processing is involved in computing `output` *Reward outcome*?\n\ni. Reward event times are converted to frame indices with `np.searchsorted` on the behavioral timestamps (and indices past the end of the truncated timestamp array are discarded). For each trial, `isreward = 1` iff at least one reward frame falls inside `[s-1, e-1)` **and** the reward zone was active at some point in that window; otherwise 0. The value is broadcast across all timepoints of the trial. Resulting rate: 84.6% rewarded / 15.8% omitted (time-weighted).\n\nii.\n```python\nrew_frames = np.searchsorted(time_v, raw['reward_times'])\nrew_frames = rew_frames[rew_frames < len(time_v)]\n...\nisreward[i] = int(bool(has_rew) and bool(in_zone))\n...\nout[5] = isreward[i]\n```\n```python\nOUTPUT_VALUES[5] = ['omitted', 'rewarded']\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5: \"per-trial `isreward` = (a reward was delivered inside the trial) AND (reward zone was entered), `behavior.get_trial_types`; broadcast in time\". Step 4 validates the rate against the paper's \"~15%\" omission: \"84.66% of trials rewarded ... Consistent (15.3%)\". Step 10 Check 5 decomposes the unrewarded trials: \"Unrewarded trials = 15.3% true omissions (zone never activated) + 0.8% lapses (zone entered, no reward); both are `reward_outcome = 0`, matching `behavior.get_trial_types`.\" Step 10 Check 2 verified this output against raw NWB reward timestamps (PASS).\n\n## 12. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Six cases are handled explicitly:\n1. **Behavior/ophys length mismatch** (10 sessions, all two-plane m17/m18, behavior one sample shorter): every stream is truncated to the common length, and trial start/teleport indices beyond the common length are dropped, keeping starts and stops paired.\n2. **Trial start at frame 0** would make `start-1` negative: `starts` is clamped with `np.maximum(starts, 1)` (and the same clamp is applied to the baseline segment starts).\n3. **Reward events past the end of the timestamp array**: `rew_frames` is filtered to valid indices.\n4. **The `environment = −1` sentinel** at out-of-lap samples: excluded before taking the per-trial median, with a fallback of 0 if no valid sample exists.\n5. **Non-finite deconvolved events inside a trial**: the trial is skipped (defensive guard; never triggered).\n6. **Degenerate trials/sessions**: trials with fewer than 2 frames and sessions with fewer than 2 usable trials are dropped.\n\nPlus the quality-control drop of 81 lick-sensor-error trials (see 1-e). Structural assumptions are asserted rather than assumed: `len(trial_starts) == len(teleports)` and `all(teleports > trial_starts)`.\n\nii.\n```python\nnB = len(d['time']); nF = d['F'].shape[1]; n = min(nB, nF)\nd['n_trunc'] = max(nB, nF) - n\nif d['n_trunc'] > 0:\n    for k in ('time', 'pos', 'speed', 'lick', 'rzone', 'env', 'trialnum', 'scanning'):\n        d[k] = d[k][:n]\n    d['F'] = d['F'][:, :n]; d['Fneu'] = d['Fneu'][:, :n]\n    d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][d['trial_starts'] < n]\n    d['teleports'] = d['teleports'][d['teleports'] < n]\n    d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][:len(d['teleports'])]\n```\n```python\nassert len(starts) == len(stops), 'trial_start / teleport count mismatch'\nassert np.all(stops > starts), 'teleport before trial start'\nstarts = np.maximum(starts, 1)\n...\nrew_frames = rew_frames[rew_frames < len(time_v)]\n...\nev = env[sl]; ev = ev[ev >= 0]\nenv_trial[i] = int(np.round(np.median(ev))) if ev.size else 0\n...\nif T < 2: continue\nif not np.all(np.isfinite(ev_trial)): continue\n...\nif len(n) < 2:\n    print(f\"  SKIPPING {info['file']}: only {len(n)} usable trials\")\n    continue\n```\n\niii. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. The AI already vectorised the one loop that mattered: the per-cell Pearson correlation in the interneuron detector was replaced by a single matrix–vector product. The remaining Python loops are all over variable-length trial segments and are inherently hard to vectorise:\n- `compute_events` runs **three** separate `for s, e in zip(starts, stops)` passes (masking, baseline, smoothing + OASIS) over ~80 segments per session. Mask everything outside the per-trial (or, on `keep_teleports` days, trial-plus-ITI) segments to NaN.\n2. Neuropil subtraction: `F - 0.7 * Fneu`.\n3. Per segment, add back `0.7 × mean(Fneu)` of that segment so the ratio is a true dF/F.\n4. Maximin baseline per segment: NaN-aware Gaussian smoothing with sigma `[0, 15]` samples → `minimum_filter1d(300)` → `maximum_filter1d(300)` (the Methods' 20 s window at 15.5 Hz).\n5. `dF/F = (F - F0) / |F0|`.\n6. 2-sample Gaussian smoothing of dF/F per segment.\n7. `suite2p.extraction.dcnv.oasis(dff, 2000, tau=0.7, fs)` per segment → \"events\".\n\n`fs` is the **per-plane** rate (`scanner rate / n_planes`), so the two-plane m17/m18 sessions use 15.5078 Hz rather than the stored 31.0156 Hz. The `keep_teleports` flag (whether the baseline window may span the teleport) is looked up per animal and experiment day from the reference `teleport_metadata.teleport_sessions` table. Planes are pooled after processing. The final `neural[session][trial]` array is `(n_neurons, n_timepoints)` float32.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_events(F, Fneu, starts, stops, fs, keep_teleports=False):\n    starts, stops = baseline_segments(starts, stops, keep_teleports)\n    f_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    fneu_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    for s, e in zip(starts, stops):\n        f_[:, s - 1:e - 1] = F[:, s - 1:e - 1]\n        fneu_[:, s - 1:e - 1] = Fneu[:, s - 1:e - 1]\n    nanmask = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * fneu_                                     # neuropil subtraction\n    flow = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    for s, e in zip(starts, stops):\n        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n        f_[:, sl] = f_[:, sl] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(fneu_[:, sl], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        seg = nansmooth(f_[:, sl], [0, BASELINE_SMOOTH])       # sigma 15\n        seg = minimum_filter1d(seg, BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)  # 300 samples ~ 20 s\n        seg = maximum_filter1d(seg, BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n        flow[:, sl] = seg\n    dff = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - flow[:, nanmask]) / np.abs(flow[:, nanmask])\n    events = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    for s, e in zip(starts, stops):\n        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n        dff[:, sl] = nansmooth(dff[:, sl], DFF_SMOOTH, axis=1)  # sigma 2\n        events[:, sl] = dcnv.oasis(np.ascontiguousarray(dff[:, sl]), 2000, TAU, fs)\n    return dff, events\n```\n\n```python\nTELEPORT_SESSIONS = {'m10': [1, 7, 8, 14, 15], ..., 'm19': [1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17]}\n\ndef baseline_segments(starts, stops, keep_teleports):\n    if keep_teleports:\n        seg_starts = np.append(starts[0], np.asarray(stops[:-1]) + 2)\n    else:\n        seg_starts = np.asarray(starts)\n    return np.maximum(seg_starts, 1), np.asarray(stops)\n\nd['fs'] = d['scan_rate'] / len(planes)     # per-plane sampling rate\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 3 quotes the Methods: per-trial maximin baseline with a 20 s sliding window, `dF/F = (F - F0)/|F0|`, 2-sample (~0.129 s) Gaussian smoothing, \"activity rate ... extracted by deconvolving dF/F ... using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p\". Parameter provenance is documented: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method='maximin'` from `preprocessing.dff`, `tau = 0.7` from \"the suite2p ops in the repo's example notebook\". Step 10 Check 3 tabulates the dF/F, deconvolution, `keep_teleports` and multi-plane steps as \"identical\" to the reference. The `keep_teleports` table was added as an explicit Step 10 fix: \"the first full conversion used `keep_teleports=False` everywhere, but the reference sets it per animal/day from `reward_relative/teleport_metadata.py` ... and all data were re-converted, re-verified, re-sanity-checked and re-trained.\"\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters, both from the paper:\n1. **`iscell`**: only ROIs with `PlaneSegmentation['iscell'][:, 0] == 1` (suite2p detection + the authors' manual curation) are kept. 138,678 of 260,091 ROIs.\n2. **Putative-interneuron exclusion**: any remaining cell whose dF/F correlates with running speed at Pearson r > 0.5 over the in-trial samples is dropped (`spatial.is_putative_interneuron`, `r_thresh = 0.5`). 390 cells (0.28%) removed.\n\nThe correlation is computed with a vectorised matrix–vector formulation rather than a per-cell loop, and cells with zero variance (NaN r) are treated as non-interneurons. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. The AI already vectorised the one loop that mattered: the per-cell Pearson correlation in the interneuron detector was replaced by a single matrix–vector product. The remaining Python loops are all over variable-length trial segments and are inherently hard to vectorise:\n- `compute_events` runs **three** separate `for s, e in zip(starts, stops)` passes (masking, baseline, smoothing + OASIS) over ~80 segments per session. How are the data split into trials?\n\ni. Trial boundaries come from the two behavioral flag series: `starts = np.where(trial_start > 0)[0]` and `stops = np.where(teleport > 0)[0]`. The trial window is the half-open frame range **`[start-1, stop-1)`**, i.e. the convention used by the reference repo itself (`preprocessing.dff` and `glmUtils.get_timeseries_data` both slice `[trial_start_inds-1 : teleport_inds-1]`). The ITI/teleport period and the teleport frame itself are excluded. Exactly the same `[s-1, e-1)` slice is used for the neural data, all inputs and all outputs, so every stream is sample-aligned. Assertions check that the number of trial starts equals the number of teleports and that every teleport follows its start; `starts` is clamped with `np.maximum(starts, 1)` so `start-1` can never be negative.\n\nii.\n```python\nd['trial_starts'] = np.where(np.asarray(beh['trial_start'].data[:]) > 0)[0]\nd['teleports']    = np.where(np.asarray(beh['teleport'].data[:]) > 0)[0]\n...\nstarts = raw['trial_starts']\nstops  = raw['teleports']\nassert len(starts) == len(stops), 'trial_start / teleport count mismatch'\nassert np.all(stops > starts), 'teleport before trial start'\n# the reference indexes [start-1:stop-1]; guard against start == 0\nstarts = np.maximum(starts, 1)\nntrials_all = len(starts)\n...\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n    T = (e - 1) - (s - 1)\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 1: \"**Trial windows**: trials run from `trial_start_inds` to `teleport_inds` (with the -1 index convention in glmUtils/dff). Four filters:\n1. **Lick-sensor-error trials are dropped**: a trial is flagged if more than 30% of its frames have a cumulative lick count > 2 (the rule stated in the paper's Methods; the repo's `glmUtils` uses 35% and `behavior.correct_lick_sensor_error` uses 50%). This flags **exactly 81** trials out of 12,216, reproducing the paper's \"n = 81 out of 12,376 trials removed\" count.\n2. Trials shorter than 2 frames are dropped (never triggered; the shortest surviving trial is 96 frames).\n3. Trials whose deconvolved events contain any non-finite value are dropped (defensive guard; never triggered).\n4. Sessions left with fewer than 2 usable trials are dropped (never triggered; minimum is 40).\n\nNo speed threshold is applied (the paper's <2 cm/s mask is deliberately not applied). 12,135 of 12,216 trials are kept.\n\nii.\n```python\nLICK_ERROR_FRAC = 0.30      # >30% of frames with cumulative lick > 2 -> lick sensor error (methods)\nLICK_ERROR_COUNT = 2\n...\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n    ...\n    lk = lick[sl]\n    lick_error[i] = lk.size > 0 and (np.sum(lk > LICK_ERROR_COUNT) / lk.size) > LICK_ERROR_FRAC\n...\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    if lick_error[i]:\n        continue                      # lick sensor error (methods): licks unusable\n    sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n    T = (e - 1) - (s - 1)\n    if T < 2:\n        continue\n    ev_trial = events[:, sl]\n    if not np.all(np.isfinite(ev_trial)):\n        continue                      # should not happen; guard against bad frames\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, Key Decision 4: \"**Trials with lick-sensor errors are dropped** (the paper NaNs their licks; we cannot store NaN in a categorical output). Rule (from methods): > 30% of frames in the trial with cumulative lick count > 2. This rule reproduces the paper's count of 81 trials exactly.\" The trajectory (step 94) records the trade-off explicitly: \"Dropping 35 trials from one session loses neural data... An alternative... keep the trials but set lick=0... would inject wrong labels. Dropping is cleaner... only 81/12,216 trials (0.66%)\". Key Decision 3 justifies *not* applying the paper's 2 cm/s speed mask: \"(a) a decoder needs contiguous, equally spaced time bins within a trial and (b) speed itself is a decoder output whose first bin is defined as < 2 cm/s, so removing those samples would delete an entire output class.\"\n\n## 2-a. What variables in the raw data is the `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. The neural data are recomputed from the **raw suite2p traces**: `processing/ophys/Fluorescence/plane*` (F) and `processing/ophys/Neuropil/plane*` (Fneu), pooled over planes along the ROI axis. The NWB `Deconvolved` series is explicitly **not** used. ROI-to-`iscell` mapping is done through the `rois` DynamicTableRegion index of each ROIResponseSeries into `ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation`.\n\nii.\n```python\nplanes = sorted(oph['Fluorescence'].roi_response_series.keys())\nFs, Fneus, roi_idx = [], [], []\nfor pl in planes:\n    rrs = oph['Fluorescence'].roi_response_series[pl]\n    Fs.append(np.asarray(rrs.data[:], dtype=np.float32))\n    Fneus.append(np.asarray(oph['Neuropil'].roi_response_series[pl].data[:], dtype=np.float32))\n    roi_idx.append(np.asarray(rrs.rois.data[:], dtype=np.int64))\nd['F']    = np.concatenate(Fs,   axis=1).T      # (n_roi, n_frames)\nd['Fneu'] = np.concatenate(Fneus, axis=1).T\nroi_idx = np.concatenate(roi_idx)\nps = oph['ImageSegmentation'].plane_segmentations['PlaneSegmentation']\niscell = np.asarray(ps['iscell'].data[:])[:, 0]\nd['iscell'] = iscell[roi_idx] == 1\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 4 documents a direct empirical test: \"NWB `Deconvolved` has no NaNs, is non-zero during the ITI and has raw-F magnitudes (mean ~96); corr with my re-implementation of the paper pipeline = 0.38 ... NWB `Deconvolved` is suite2p's own `spks` on raw F, **not** the paper's `events`. I recompute dF/F + OASIS from the NWB `Fluorescence` and `Neuropil` exactly as in `preprocessing.dff()`.\" Step 1 notes that the paper's Fig. 3 decoder and its GLM both consume `sess.timeseries['events']`, which `utilities.multi_anim_sess` produces by calling `preprocessing.dff(..., deconvolve=True)` on F/Fneu. Methods \"planes were pooled for all analyses\" justifies concatenating planes.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. A faithful port of `reward_relative.preprocessing.dff(..., deconvolve=True)`, run per plane at that plane's own sampling rate:\n1. Mask everything outside the per-trial (or, on `keep_teleports` days, trial-plus-ITI) segments to NaN.\n2. Neuropil subtraction: `F - 0.7 * Fneu`.\n3. Per segment, add back `0.7 × mean(Fneu)` of that segment so the ratio is a true dF/F.\n4. Maximin baseline per segment: NaN-aware Gaussian smoothing with sigma `[0, 15]` samples → `minimum_filter1d(300)` → `maximum_filter1d(300)` (the Methods' 20 s window at 15.5 Hz).\n5. `dF/F = (F - F0) / |F0|`.\n6. 2-sample Gaussian smoothing of dF/F per segment.\n7. `suite2p.extraction.dcnv.oasis(dff, 2000, tau=0.7, fs)` per segment → \"events\".\n\n`fs` is the **per-plane** rate (`scanner rate / n_planes`), so the two-plane m17/m18 sessions use 15.5078 Hz rather than the stored 31.0156 Hz. The `keep_teleports` flag (whether the baseline window may span the teleport) is looked up per animal and experiment day from the reference `teleport_metadata.teleport_sessions` table. Planes are pooled after processing. The final `neural[session][trial]` array is `(n_neurons, n_timepoints)` float32.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_events(F, Fneu, starts, stops, fs, keep_teleports=False):\n    starts, stops = baseline_segments(starts, stops, keep_teleports)\n    f_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    fneu_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    for s, e in zip(starts, stops):\n        f_[:, s - 1:e - 1] = F[:, s - 1:e - 1]\n        fneu_[:, s - 1:e - 1] = Fneu[:, s - 1:e - 1]\n    nanmask = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * fneu_                                     # neuropil subtraction\n    flow = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    for s, e in zip(starts, stops):\n        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n        f_[:, sl] = f_[:, sl] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(fneu_[:, sl], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        seg = nansmooth(f_[:, sl], [0, BASELINE_SMOOTH])       # sigma 15\n        seg = minimum_filter1d(seg, BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)  # 300 samples ~ 20 s\n        seg = maximum_filter1d(seg, BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n        flow[:, sl] = seg\n    dff = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - flow[:, nanmask]) / np.abs(flow[:, nanmask])\n    events = np.full(F.shape, np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n    for s, e in zip(starts, stops):\n        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n        dff[:, sl] = nansmooth(dff[:, sl], DFF_SMOOTH, axis=1)  # sigma 2\n        events[:, sl] = dcnv.oasis(np.ascontiguousarray(dff[:, sl]), 2000, TAU, fs)\n    return dff, events\n```\n\n```python\nTELEPORT_SESSIONS = {'m10': [1, 7, 8, 14, 15], ..., 'm19': [1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17]}\n\ndef baseline_segments(starts, stops, keep_teleports):\n    if keep_teleports:\n        seg_starts = np.append(starts[0], np.asarray(stops[:-1]) + 2)\n    else:\n        seg_starts = np.asarray(starts)\n    return np.maximum(seg_starts, 1), np.asarray(stops)\n\nd['fs'] = d['scan_rate'] / len(planes)     # per-plane sampling rate\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 3 quotes the Methods: per-trial maximin baseline with a 20 s sliding window, `dF/F = (F - F0)/|F0|`, 2-sample (~0.129 s) Gaussian smoothing, \"activity rate ... extracted by deconvolving dF/F ... using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p\". Parameter provenance is documented: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method='maximin'` from `preprocessing.dff`, `tau = 0.7` from \"the suite2p ops in the repo's example notebook\". Step 10 Check 3 tabulates the dF/F, deconvolution, `keep_teleports` and multi-plane steps as \"identical\" to the reference. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. From the per-trial rewarded flag `isreward`, which is computed from **two** raw variables following `reward_relative.behavior.get_trial_types`: the `Reward` event series' own `timestamps` (mapped to frame indices with `np.searchsorted` on the behavioral timestamps), **and** the `reward_zone` behavioral series. A trial counts as rewarded only if a reward event fell inside the trial window *and* the reward zone was entered during that trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nd['rzone'] = np.asarray(beh['reward_zone'].data[:], dtype=np.float64)\nd['reward_times'] = np.asarray(beh['Reward'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n...\nrew_frames = np.searchsorted(time_v, raw['reward_times'])\nrew_frames = rew_frames[rew_frames < len(time_v)]\n...\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n    sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n    has_rew = np.any((rew_frames >= s - 1) & (rew_frames < e - 1))\n    in_zone = np.any(rzone[sl] > 0)\n    isreward[i] = int(bool(has_rew) and bool(in_zone))\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 1 identifies `get_trial_types` as producing \"Per-trial `isreward` (reward>0 AND rzone>0 within trial)\"; Step 5 maps output 5 / input 3 to that same definition. Step 2 documents `Reward` as \"an **event series**: one 0.004 mL sample per delivered reward, with timestamps\", i.e. it is not on the frame clock, hence `searchsorted`. Step 4 checks the resulting rate against the paper: \"`get_trial_types`: rewarded = reward>0 AND rzone>0 in trial | 84.66% of trials rewarded | '~15%' omission | Consistent (15.3%).\"\n\n## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Previous trial outcome*?\n\ni. For trial `i`, the input is `isreward[i-1]`; for the first trial of a session (`i == 0`) it is set to 0. The index runs over *all* detected trials, so the \"previous trial\" is the true preceding lap even when that lap was dropped for a lick-sensor error. The scalar is broadcast across the trial's timepoints.\n\nii.\n```python\ninp[3] = isreward[i - 1] if i > 0 else 0\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, Key Decision 6: \"**Previous-trial outcome for the first trial of a session = 0**. There is no preceding trial in the imaged session (mice did run ~30 un-imaged warm-up trials beforehand, but those data are not in the file), so the most conservative encoding is 'not rewarded'; this affects 152 of 12,135 trials (1.3%).\" This matches the Decoder Task's \"Previous trial outcome (binary, omitted = 0, rewarded = 1, per trial)\".\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. From the `position` behavioral series combined with the per-trial reward-zone boundaries. The zone identity for each trial is reconstructed the way the reference code does it — from the **scene name** embedded in the NWB `identifier` (e.g. `/data/InVivoDA/GCAMP11/23_02_2023/Env1_LocationB_to_A`) plus the switch-at-trial-30 rule, a port of `reward_relative.behavior.get_reward_zones`. Zone coordinates are the paper's: A = 80–130, B = 200–250, C = 320–370 cm.\n\nii.\n```python\nZONE_DICT = {'A': (80.0, 130.0), 'B': (200.0, 250.0), 'C': (320.0, 370.0)}\nCHANGE_TRIAL = 30           # reward zone switches after 30 trials (methods)\n\ndef get_reward_zone_labels(scene, ntrials, change_trial=CHANGE_TRIAL):\n    \"\"\"Per-trial reward zone label, replicating reward_relative.behavior.get_reward_zones.\"\"\"\n    if scene.endswith('LocationA'):\n        return ['A'] * ntrials\n    if scene.endswith('LocationB'):\n        return ['B'] * ntrials\n    if scene.endswith('LocationC'):\n        return ['C'] * ntrials\n    for first in ('A', 'B', 'C'):\n        if f'{first}_to' in scene:\n            second = scene[-1]\n            if second not in ZONE_DICT:\n                raise ValueError(f'unrecognised switch scene {scene}')\n            n0 = min(change_trial, ntrials)\n            return [first] * n0 + [second] * (ntrials - n0)\n    raise ValueError(f'unrecognised scene {scene}')\n```\n\n```python\nd['scene'] = nwb.identifier.split('/')[-1]\n...\nlabels = get_reward_zone_labels(raw['scene'], ntrials_all)\n...\nzlab = labels[i]\nz0, z1 = ZONE_DICT[zlab]\nrz_cat, _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 1 identifies `get_reward_zones` as the reference function: \"Per-trial reward zone [start,stop] cm and label from scene name. Zones used in this experiment: A = [80,130], B = [200,250], C = [320,370]; switch days change zone at trial 30\". Step 2 notes that the NWB `identifier` preserves the original scene string. Crucially, Step 4 reports an end-to-end validation against the data: \"reconstructing zone labels from the scene name in `identifier` (reference logic) matched the zone position observed in the data on **every one of the 12,216 trials** (0 mismatches).\" The trajectory (step 39) records the direct observation that confirmed the trial-30 rule: \"trial 0-29 = reward zone b (~200-250), trial 30+ = zone a (~80-130), confirming change at trial index 30 (0-indexed), matching change_trial=30 in get_reward_zones.\"\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. A signed linear distance to the **nearest point** of the reward zone: negative before the zone (`pos − zone_start`), exactly 0 anywhere inside `[zone_start, zone_end]`, positive after (`pos − zone_end`). This continuous value is then discretized (see 7-c). The continuous distance itself is not stored (only used for the `--show-processing` plots).\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_reward_distance(pos, zone_start, zone_end):\n    \"\"\"Signed distance to the nearest point of the reward zone -> 7 categories.\"\"\"\n    d = np.zeros_like(pos)\n    before = pos < zone_start\n    after = pos > zone_end\n    d[before] = pos[before] - zone_start          # negative: before the zone\n    d[after] = pos[after] - zone_end              # positive: past the zone\n    ...\n    return cat, d\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5 outputs table: \"signed distance to the **nearest point of the reward zone**: `d = pos - zone_start` if `pos < zone_start`; `d = 0` if inside `[zone_start, zone_end]`; `d = pos - zone_end` if `pos > zone_end`.\" Step 1 notes the deviation from the reference's own variable: \"**Reward-relative position**: `rel_pos` = position minus reward-zone start, either linear (wrapped into [0,450)) or circular ... The Decoder Task here asks for *linear* distance in cm to the nearest point of the reward zone, so we adapt.\" Step 10 Check 3(f) records this as a \"deviation required by task\".\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Seven categories assigned by explicit boolean masks, matching the Decoder Task's bins: `d < −50` → 0; `−50 ≤ d < −10` → 1; `−10 ≤ d < 0` → 2; `d == 0` → 3 (i.e. inside the zone); `0 < d ≤ 10` → 4; `10 < d ≤ 50` → 5; `d > 50` → 6.\n\nii.\n```python\ncat = np.zeros(pos.shape, dtype=np.int64)\ncat[d < -50] = 0\ncat[(d >= -50) & (d < -10)] = 1\ncat[(d >= -10) & (d < 0)] = 2\ncat[d == 0] = 3\ncat[(d > 0) & (d <= 10)] = 4\ncat[(d > 10) & (d <= 50)] = 5\ncat[d > 50] = 6\n```\n```python\nOUTPUT_VALUES[0] = ['< -50 cm', '-50 to -10 cm', '-10 to 0 cm', 'in reward zone (0 cm)',\n                    '0 to +10 cm', '+10 to +50 cm', '> +50 cm']\n```\n\niii. The edges are taken verbatim from the Decoder Task specification; category 3 is defined as exactly 0, which by construction is the set of samples inside the reward zone. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5 planned the check \"`reward_zone_distance == 3` (distance 0) occurs for exactly the samples with position inside the zone\", and Step 10 Check 2 reports an independent re-derivation with `np.select` passing. The resulting distribution [0.256, 0.102, 0.073, 0.238, 0.021, 0.072, 0.238] was checked for full class coverage.\n\n## 7-d. No separate alignment: `position` is sliced with the same `[s-1, e-1)` index range as the neural events, so distance categories are sample-for-sample aligned with the neural matrix.\n\nii.\n```python\nsl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\nev_trial = events[:, sl]\np = pos[sl]\n...\nrz_cat, _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\nout[0] = rz_cat\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5: \"per-trial `isreward` = (a reward was delivered inside the trial) AND (reward zone was entered), `behavior.get_trial_types`; broadcast in time\".
