How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Six cases are handled explicitly:\n1. **Behavior/ophys length mismatch** (10 sessions, all two-plane m17/m18, behavior one sample shorter): every stream is truncated to the common length, and trial start/teleport indices beyond the common length are dropped, keeping starts and stops paired.\n2. **Trial start at frame 0** would make `start-1` negative: `starts` is clamped with `np.maximum(starts, 1)` (and the same clamp is applied to the baseline segment starts).\n3. **Reward events past the end of the timestamp array**: `rew_frames` is filtered to valid indices.\n4. **The `environment = −1` sentinel** at out-of-lap samples: excluded before taking the per-trial median, with a fallback of 0 if no valid sample exists.\n5. **Non-finite deconvolved events inside a trial**: the trial is skipped (defensive guard; never triggered).\n6. **Degenerate trials/sessions**: trials with fewer than 2 frames and sessions with fewer than 2 usable trials are dropped.\n\nPlus the quality-control drop of 81 lick-sensor-error trials (see 1-e). Structural assumptions are asserted rather than assumed: `len(trial_starts) == len(teleports)` and `all(teleports > trial_starts)`.\n\nii.\n```python\nnB = len(d['time']); nF = d['F'].shape[1]; n = min(nB, nF)\nd['n_trunc'] = max(nB, nF) - n\nif d['n_trunc'] > 0:\n    for k in ('time', 'pos', 'speed', 'lick', 'rzone', 'env', 'trialnum', 'scanning'):\n        d[k] = d[k][:n]\n    d['F'] = d['F'][:, :n]; d['Fneu'] = d['Fneu'][:, :n]\n    d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][d['trial_starts'] < n]\n    d['teleports'] = d['teleports'][d['teleports'] < n]\n    d['trial_starts'] = d['trial_starts'][:len(d['teleports'])]\n```\n```python\nassert len(starts) == len(stops), 'trial_start / teleport count mismatch'\nassert np.all(stops > starts), 'teleport before trial start'\nstarts = np.maximum(starts, 1)\n...\nrew_frames = rew_frames[rew_frames < len(time_v)]\n...\nev = env[sl]; ev = ev[ev >= 0]\nenv_trial[i] = int(np.round(np.median(ev))) if ev.size else 0\n...\nif T < 2: continue\nif not np.all(np.isfinite(ev_trial)): continue\n...\nif len(n) < 2:\n    print(f\"  SKIPPING {info['file']}: only {len(n)} usable trials\")\n    continue\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 9 documents the length-mismatch discovery and fix (\"the 'one frame correction ... scan stopping mid frame' case the reference alignment code warns about ... no trial is affected because all `trial_start`/`teleport` indices are inside the shorter array\"). Step 10 Check 5 is a dedicated edge-case audit (`/app/cache/check_edges.py`) reporting: no `trial_start` at frame 0; start/teleport counts equal in all 152 sessions; the 10 truncated sessions; no switch session with ≤ 30 trials; environment changes only at trial boundaries; no session with < 2 usable trials (minimum 40); and \"Position = -500 (pre-scanning) never occurs inside a trial window.\"\n\n## 13-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. The script prints per-session timings (`t_load`, `t_dff`, `t_total`). Measured on the full run:\n1. **dF/F + OASIS deconvolution** (`compute_events`) — dominant: 0.3 s on the smallest session up to ~20 s on the largest (4174 ROIs); roughly 3–4× the load time on typical sessions.\n2. **NWB reading** of the full `Fluorescence`/`Neuropil` arrays — I/O bound, 0.3–3.0 s per session.\n3. **Pickling** the 9.63 GB output — 9.7 s.\n4. Per-trial assembly and the interneuron correlation are negligible.\n\nWith 12 parallel worker processes, all 152 sessions complete in **130 s** wall clock (plus ~10 s to write the pickle), far under the 15-minute target.\n\nii.\n```python\nt_start = time.time()\nraw = read_nwb_session(path)\nt_load = time.time() - t_start\n...\nt0 = time.time()\ndff, events = compute_events(F, Fneu, starts, stops, raw['fs'], keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\nt_dff = time.time() - t0\n...\nprint(f\"  {info['file']}: ... load {t_load:.1f}s dff {t_dff:.1f}s total {info['t_total']:.1f}s\", flush=True)\n```\n```python\nctx = mp.get_context('spawn')\nwith ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nw, mp_context=ctx) as ex:\n    for res in ex.map(_worker, remaining):\n        results.append(res)\nprint(f'all sessions processed in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s')\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 6: \"Loading the full `Fluorescence`/`Neuropil` arrays is the main I/O cost (0.3-1.5 s/session).\" Step 7 Run Time Estimates table: \"NWB load ... ~3 min serial; dF/F + OASIS ... ~12 min serial; assembly + pickling ... ~2 min; **Total (12 workers) ~2-4 min**\". Step 9 confirms the realised time: \"152 sessions, 12 workers, **131 s** wall clock, well under the 15 min target.\"\n\n## 13-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. The AI already vectorised the one loop that mattered: the per-cell Pearson correlation in the interneuron detector was replaced by a single matrix–vector product. The remaining Python loops are all over variable-length trial segments and are inherently hard to vectorise:\n- `compute_events` runs **three** separate `for s, e in zip(starts, stops)` passes (masking, baseline, smoothing + OASIS) over ~80 segments per session. These could at least be fused, and the masking pass could be replaced by a single boolean mask built with `np.add.reduceat`/index arithmetic instead of a per-trial slice assignment.\n- The per-trial `isreward`/`lick_error`/`env_trial` loop computes three reductions per trial; these could be done for the whole session with `np.add.reduceat` over the trial boundaries.\n- The per-trial assembly loop calls `np.digitize` on each trial's position and speed separately; both could be applied once to the whole session array and then sliced.\n- `dcnv.oasis` is called per segment — this one genuinely cannot be merged, because the deconvolution must not run across trial boundaries.\n\nii.\n```python\n# vectorised (was a per-cell python loop):\ndm_c = dm - dm.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\nsp_c = sp - sp.mean()\ndenom = np.sqrt((dm_c ** 2).sum(axis=1) * (sp_c ** 2).sum())\nspeed_corr = (dm_c @ sp_c) / denom\n```\n```python\n# remaining per-segment loops in compute_events:\nfor s, e in zip(starts, stops):          # pass 1: mask\n    f_[:, s - 1:e - 1] = F[:, s - 1:e - 1]\n    fneu_[:, s - 1:e - 1] = Fneu[:, s - 1:e - 1]\nfor s, e in zip(starts, stops):          # pass 2: neuropil mean + maximin baseline\n    ...\nfor s, e in zip(starts, stops):          # pass 3: smoothing + OASIS\n    ...\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 6: \"Code inefficiencies identified: ... The interneuron speed correlation was originally a per-cell python loop -> replaced by a vectorised matrix-vector correlation. Code speedups added: Vectorised correlation for interneuron detection; float32 throughout; `dcnv.oasis` called once per trial on a contiguous array; Multiprocessing over sessions (12 workers, each session is independent).\" The AI's position is that the remaining per-segment loops are required by the reference algorithm (per-trial baselines and per-trial deconvolution) and are cheap relative to the filtering/OASIS work inside them; Step 7 shows the resulting time was already well within budget.\n\n## 13-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. Within `compute_events`, the trial-segment loop is walked **three times** over the same `(starts, stops)` pairs, so the slice arithmetic and the traversal of the full `(n_roi, n_frames)` arrays happen three times instead of once (passes 2 and 3 could be fused). The trial loop is also walked twice in `convert_session` — once to compute `isreward` / `lick_error` / `env_trial` for all trials, and once to assemble the kept trials — because the \"previous trial outcome\" input needs the outcome of trials that may themselves be dropped. `np.searchsorted(time, reward_times)` is computed once in `convert_session` and again inside `make_processing_plots`, and `discretize_reward_distance` is recomputed in the plotting function for the plotted trials.\n\nNotably, the code does **not** repeat the expensive part: unlike a survey-then-convert design, each NWB file is opened and read exactly once for the whole conversion.\n\nii.\n```python\n# three passes over the same segments\nfor s, e in zip(starts, stops):  ...   # mask\nfor s, e in zip(starts, stops):  ...   # baseline\nfor s, e in zip(starts, stops):  ...   # smooth + oasis\n\n# two passes over trials\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):   # isreward / lick_error / env_trial\n    ...\nfor i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):   # assembly\n    ...\n```\n```python\n# recomputed inside the plotting helper\nrf = np.searchsorted(raw['time'], raw['reward_times'])\n...\n_, d = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\n```\n\niii. The two-pass trial structure is a deliberate consequence of the `previous_trial_outcome` input and of the lick-error filter: the outcome of trial `i-1` must be known even if trial `i-1` is not emitted (CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, inputs table). The repeated work in `make_processing_plots` only runs under `--show-processing` for at most 2 sessions. The AI's documented efficiency effort (Step 6/7) focused on the dominant costs — the dF/F/OASIS pipeline and per-session parallelism — and the realised 130 s runtime made further deduplication unnecessary.\n\n## 13-d. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n\nii.\n```python\ndff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n```\n\niii. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n```python\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n        continue\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n```\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n```python\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n                    'B': [200, 250],\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\n...\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n```\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n```python\npstay = .9\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n```\n\niii. I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. Derived from the `lick` behavior time series.\n\nii.\n```python\nlicks = behavior_data['lick'].data[:][:T]\nassert np.allclose(behavior_data['lick'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for lick do not match trial number timestamps\"\n...\nlicks_curr = licks[idx]\n```\n\niii. The `lick` variable records lick events at each timepoint.\n\n## 9-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Lick*?\n\ni. Binarized: any positive lick value is mapped to 1, otherwise 0.\n\nii.\n```python\noutput_curr[3] = (licks_curr > 0).astype(int)\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify binary output (no/yes). The raw lick values can be >1, so thresholding at >0 converts to binary.\n\n## 9-c. How is `output` *Lick* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Same time indices as the neural data within each trial — no additional alignment needed.\n\nii. Same indexing as neural: `licks_curr = licks[idx]`\n\niii. Verified by timestamp assertions.\n\n## 10-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Reward zone location* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `reward_zone` behavior time series and `position` behavior time series, as described in answer 7-a. \n\nii. See answer 7-a.\n\niii. See answer 7-a.\n\n## 10-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Reward zone location*?\n\ni. See answer 7-a. \n\nii. See answer 7-a.\n\niii. See answer 7-a. \n\n## 11-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Reward outcome* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `Reward` behavior time series. Reward events have their own timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_times = behavior_data['Reward'].timestamps[:]\nreward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\nisreward = np.zeros(T)\nisreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n...\noutput_curr[5] = np.any(isreward[idx]).astype(int)\n```\n\niii. The `Reward` time series records reward delivery events with separate timestamps from the behavior sampling rate.\n\n## 11-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Reward outcome*?\n\ni. Reward event timestamps are mapped to the nearest behavior timepoint using `searchsorted`. For each trial, the output is 1 if any reward event occurred within the trial, 0 otherwise. The value is constant across all timepoints in the trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\nerr = timestamps[reward_time_indices] - reward_times\nassert np.all(np.abs(err) <= time_bin_size/2)\nisreward = np.zeros(T)\nisreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n...\noutput_curr[5] = np.any(isreward[idx]).astype(int)\n```\n\niii. The alignment error is checked to be within half a time bin. `np.any` is used because a trial either was rewarded or not — the specific timepoint doesn't matter for the per-trial binary output.\n\n## 12. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Several cases are handled:\n- **Neural/behavior length mismatch**: If the number of neural time bins differs from behavior timestamps, data is cropped to the minimum of the two with a warning printed.\n- **Short trials**: Trials with fewer than 50 timepoints (`min_ntimepoints`) are skipped with a warning.\n- **Missing reward zone data**: Trials where `reward_zone` is never active (all zeros) get NaN positions, and the Viterbi algorithm handles these via uniform emission (assignment driven by neighboring trials' transitions).\n- **Reward timestamp alignment**: An assertion verifies reward times align within half a time bin of behavior timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\nif T != len(timestamps):\n    print(f\"Warning: number of neural time bins ({T}) does not match number of behavior timestamps ({len(timestamps)}), cropping to the minimum of the two\")\n    T = min(T, len(timestamps))\n    spike_data = spike_data[:T]\n    timestamps = timestamps[:T]\n...\nif idx.sum() < min_ntimepoints:\n    print(f\"Skipping trial {trial}...\")\n    istrial[trial] = False\n    continue\n```\n\niii. These are defensive checks found during data exploration. The neural/behavior mismatch occurs in a small number of sessions.\n\n## 13-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. The most time-consuming steps are:\n1. **Loading NWB files** (`pynwb.NWBHDF5IO` and reading large arrays) — I/O bound\n2. **The survey step** — loads every NWB file to gather statistics and reward zone positions\n3. **Full conversion** — loads every NWB file again and extracts all trial data\n4. **Saving the .pkl file**\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. The NWB files are large (contain full neural recordings). Conversion is otherwise quite fast\n\n## 13-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. The per-trial loop in `convert_session_data` (lines 267-332) iterates over each trial sequentially. Some operations like `np.digitize` and `compute_distance_to_reward_zone` could theoretically be applied to the full session arrays before splitting into trials, but the variable trial lengths make this awkward. The Viterbi inner loop (lines 503-507) iterates over states, which could be vectorized with matrix operations.\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. The per-trial loop is the natural structure given variable-length trials. Vectorizing would require padding or masking.\n\n## 13-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. The survey step and the conversion step both load every NWB file and read the same data arrays (neural, behavior). The survey reads neural data to count neurons and check rates, then the conversion reads it again. The `reward_zone_positions` are computed in the survey and then used in the conversion, but other data (position, speed, lick, etc.) is read twice. \n\nii. N/A\n\niii. I don't think these could be run at the same time, as it would require too much RAM. The Viterbi output created during surveying is required to process the data. It was convenient to run the survey before deciding how to handle the conversion of the data. \n\n## 13-d. What unnecessary processing does the code do that is discarded in downstream analyses?\n\ni. find nans\n    nan_inds = np.isnan(a)\n    a_nanless = np.copy(a)\n    # make nans 0\n    a_nanless[nan_inds] = 0\n\n    # inversely weight nanned indices\n    one = np.ones(a.shape)\n    one[nan_inds] = .001\n    a_nanless = ndimage.gaussian_filter(a_nanless, sig) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n    one = ndimage.gaussian_filter(one, sig) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n    return a_nanless / one\n\n\ndef nansmooth_1d(a, sig, axis=-1, return_nans=False, **kwargs):\n    \"\"\"\n    apply Gaussian smoothing to matrix A containing nans with kernel sig\n    without propagating nans\n    :param a:\n    :param sig:\n    :return:\n\n    ** copied from src/reward_relative/utilities.py::nansmooth **\n    (renamed: the TwoPUtils N-D version above already occupies the name `nansmooth`)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # was filters.gaussian_filter\n    one = ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(one, sig, axis=axis, **kwargs) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n\n    out = a_nanless / one\n    if return_nans:\n        out[nan_inds] = np.nan\n\n    return out\n\ndef dff(f,\n        trial_starts,\n        teleports,\n        f_neu=None,\n        neuropil_method=None,\n        baseline_method='maximin',\n        subtract_baseline=True,\n        neu_coef=0.7,\n        tau=0.7,\n        frame_rate=15,\n        n_planes=1,\n        deconvolve=False,\n        keep_teleports=False):\n    \"\"\"\n    Calculate dFF for 1 channel\n\n    :param f: ROI fluorescence timeseries\n    :param trial_starts:\n    :param teleports:\n    :param f_neu: neuropil fluorescence timeseries\n    :param baseline_method:\n    :param subtract_baseline: True gives ∆F/F, False just normalizes F to the basline (divides only)\n    :param neu_coef:\n    :param deconvolve: whether to deconvolve the dff trace into \"events\" (psuedo spikes)\n    :return: dff and spks if deconvolve is True, otherwise just dff\n\n    `trial_starts` and `teleports` must be pandas Series: the keep_teleports branch calls\n    `.to_list()` on `teleports`, which a numpy array does not have.      in_zone = np.any(rzone[sl] > 0)\n        isreward[i] = int(bool(has_rew) and bool(in_zone))\n        lk = lick[sl]\n        lick_error[i] = lk.size > 0 and (np.sum(lk > LICK_ERROR_COUNT) / lk.size) > LICK_ERROR_FRAC\n        ev = env[sl]\n        ev = ev[ev >= 0]\n        env_trial[i] = int(np.round(np.median(ev))) if ev.size else 0\n\n    # --- assemble trials ---------------------------------------------------------------\n    neural, inputs, outputs = [], [], []\n    kept_trials = []\n    for i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, stops)):\n        if lick_error[i]:\n            continue                      # lick sensor error (methods): licks unusable\n        sl = slice(s - 1, e - 1)\n        T = (e - 1) - (s - 1)\n        if T < 2:\n            continue\n        ev_trial = events[:, sl]\n        if not np.all(np.isfinite(ev_trial)):\n            continue                      # should not happen; guard against bad frames\n\n        p = pos[sl]\n        sp_t = speed_all[sl]\n        lk = lick[sl]\n\n        zlab = labels[i]\n        z0, z1 = ZONE_DICT[zlab]\n\n        # inputs\n        t_rel = time_v[sl] - time_v[s - 1]\n        inp = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.float32)\n        inp[0] = t_rel\n        inp[1] = env_trial[i]\n        inp[2] = i\n        inp[3] = isreward[i - 1] if i > 0 else 0\n\n        # outputs\n        rz_cat, _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, z0, z1)\n        pos_cat = np.digitize(p, POS_EDGES).astype(np.int64)\n        spd_cat = np.digitize(sp_t, SPEED_EDGES).astype(np.int64)\n        lick_cat = (lk > 0).astype(np.int64)\n        out = np.empty((6, T), dtype=np.int64)\n        out[0] = rz_cat\n        out[1] = pos_cat\n        out[2] = spd_cat\n        out[3] = lick_cat\n        out[4] = zone_code[zlab]\n        out[5] = isreward[i]\n\n        neural.append(np.ascontiguousarray(ev_trial, dtype=np.float32))\n        inputs.append(inp)\n        outputs.append(out)\n        kept_trials.append(i)\n\n    info = dict(\n        file=os.path.basename(path), subject=raw['subject'], scene=raw['scene'],\n        date=raw['date'], identifier=raw['identifier'],\n        session_start_time=raw['session_start_time'],\n        brain_region=raw['brain_region'], n_planes=raw['n_planes'], fs=raw['fs'],\n        n_roi_total=int(raw['iscell'].size), n_iscell=int(raw['iscell'].sum()),\n        n_interneurons=int(is_int.sum()), n_neurons=n_neurons,\n        n_trials_total=ntrials_all, n_trials_kept=len(neural),\n        n_lick_error=int(lick_error.sum()), n_trunc=int(raw['n_trunc']),\n        exp_day=exp_day, keep_teleports=bool(keep_teleports),\n        frac_rewarded=float(isreward.mean()),\n        is_switch='_to_' in raw['scene'],\n        kept_trials=kept_trials,\n        t_load=t_load, t_dff=t_dff, t_total=time.time() - t_start,\n    )\n    if verbose:\n        print(f\"  {info['file']}: {info['n_neurons']} neurons \"\n              f\"({info['n_iscell']} iscell, {info['n_interneurons']} interneurons), \"\n              f\"{info['n_trials_kept']}/{info['n_trials_total']} trials, \"\n              f\"load {t_load:.1f}s dff {t_dff:.1f}s total {info['t_total']:.1f}s\", flush=True)\n\n    if show_processing:\n        make_processing_plots(path, raw, dff, events, keep_cells, starts, stops,\n                              labels, isreward, neural, inputs, outputs, kept_trials, info)\n    return neural, inputs, outputs, info\n\n\n# GiocomoLab/Sosa_et_al_2024 (Sosa, Plitt, Giocomo 2025, Nat Neuro).\nPipeline (docs/preprocessing_guide.md): suite2p motion correction + ROI detection + manual curation (iscell)\n-> `sess` class (TwoPUtils) aligning VR (Unity/SQLite) to 2P frames -> `multi_anim_sess` (computes dF/F, deconvolved\n\"events\", place cells, trial sets) -> `dayData` (reward-relative cell analyses).\n\n### Key Functions Identified\n| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |\n|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| `create_sess` / `append_session_data` | src/reward_relative/preprocessing.py | LOADING | Build sess: scan info, VR alignment (`sess.align_VR_to_2P` = TwoPUtils `vr_align_to_2P`), suite2p F/Fneu, behavior timeseries (licks, rewards, speed) |\n| `vr_align_to_mock_2P` | preprocessing.py | PROCESSING | Shows exactly how VR variables are resampled to the 2P frame clock: pos/t linear-interp; morph/trialnum nearest; dz/lick/reward/tstart/teleport/rzone cumulative-sum-interp then diff; speed = smoothed dz/dt; lick rate = smoothed lick/dt |\n| `dff` | preprocessing.py | PROCESSING | dF/F per ROI: neuropil subtract (neu_coef 0.7), per-trial maximin baseline (smooth sigma 15 frames, min then max filter 300 frames), dF/F = (F-F0)/|F0|, smooth 2 frames, optional OASIS deconvolution -> `events` (spks) |\n| `multi_anim_sess` | utilities.py | PROCESSING/CURATION | Runs dff (baseline maximin, neuropil subtract, deconvolve=True -> `events`), then behavior.get_trial_types, get_reward_zones, define_trial_subsets, place-cell shuffles |\n| `get_trial_types` | behavior.py | PROCESSING | Per-trial `isreward` (reward>0 AND rzone>0 within trial) and `morph` (0=Env1, 1=Env2) |\n| `get_reward_zones` | behavior.py | PROCESSING | Per-trial reward zone [start,stop] cm and label from scene name. Zones used in this experiment: A = [80,130], B = [200,250], C = [320,370]; switch days change zone at trial 30 (`change_reward_trial`) |\n| `define_trial_subsets` | behavior.py | PROCESSING | Trial set 0 / set 1 (pre/post reward-zone switch) |\n| `get_omission_trials`, `get_omission_inds` | rewardAnalysis.py | PROCESSING | Unrewarded trials where the reward zone was never active (\"true omissions\") vs lapses |\n| `get_timeseries_data` | glmUtils.py | PROCESSING (decoder input!) | Builds the continuous time-series used for the paper's decoder/GLM: neural = deconvolved `events`; behavior = trials, rel_pos (circular distance to reward), pos, speed, licks, rewards; masks samples with speed < 2 cm/s and lick-sensor errors; trial windows are `[trial_start_inds-1 : teleport_inds-1]` |\n| `train_vs_test_blocks`, `CircularRegression` | decode.py | ANALYSIS | Paper's decoder of circular reward-relative position from deconvolved activity |\n| `define_anim_list`, `max_anim_list` | dayData.py | CURATION | Animal lists per experiment day; GCAMP2/5/6/10 excluded from switch analyses (they never had a reward switch) |\n| `sessions_dict.py` | - | METADATA | Per-animal list of sessions: date, scene (e.g. Env1_LocationA, Env1_LocationA_to_C, Env1_B_to_Env2_C), session/scan number, exp_day (1-14) |\n\n### Notes\n- **Neural signal for the decoder**: the paper's Fig. 3 decoder and the GLM both use the *deconvolved* activity\n  (`sess.timeseries['events']`, produced by suite2p OASIS `dcnv.oasis` on smoothed dF/F). dF/F (`dff`) is used for\n  place-field quantification.\n- **Speed threshold**: `get_timeseries_data(..., use_speed_thr=2)` -> samples with speed < 2 cm/s are dropped\n  (NaN-masked) in the paper's decoding analysis. For our decoder we need contiguous fixed-bin time series per trial,\n  so dropping samples would break temporal alignment; decision deferred to Step 5.\n- **Trial windows**: trials run from `trial_start_inds` to `teleport_inds` (with the -1 index convention in\n  glmUtils/dff). ITIs (post-teleport) are excluded from dF/F baseline and from the decoder data.\n- **Reward-relative position**: `rel_pos` = position minus reward-zone start, either linear (wrapped into [0,450))\n  or circular (converted to radians and wrapped to [-pi,pi]). The Decoder Task here asks for *linear* distance in cm\n  to the nearest point of the reward zone, so we adapt.\n- Lick sensor error correction: if >35% of samples in a trial have cumulative lick count > 2, the trial's licks are\n  set to NaN (glmUtils) / `correct_lick_sensor_error` in behavior.py (threshold 0.5).\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\n`/app/data/` = DANDI dandiset 001361 (Sosa, Plitt & Giocomo 2025), one directory per subject,\none NWB file per session: `sub-<id>/sub-<id>_ses-<NN>_behavior+ophys.nwb` (87 GB total, 152 files).\n\nNWB contents (verified with `pynwb`):\n- `identifier` = original path, e.g. `/data/InVivoDA/GCAMP11/23_02_2023/Env1_LocationB_to_A`\n  -> gives animal (GCAMPnn), date, and **scene** (needed for the reward-zone lookup used by the reference code).\n- `session_start_time`, `subject` (subject_id m3...m19, species, sex).\n- `acquisition/TwoPhotonSeries` (link to raw movie; Both \"stay\" and \"switch\" days are included:\n  the decoder task asks for environment, trial number, reward-zone identity and reward outcome, all of which are\n  defined on every session.\n- **subjects**: `nwb.subject.subject_id` -> ['m3','m4','m7','m11','m12','m13','m14','m15','m17','m18','m19'].\n- **brain_regions**: `['CA1']` (imaging plane location \"hippocampus, CA1\" for every session); `brain_region_idx`\n  = zeros(n_neurons) per session.\n\n### Neural data\n| Step | Implementation | Reference |\n|---|---|---|\n| Load F, Fneu | `processing/ophys/Fluorescence`, `Neuropil`, all planes concatenated along the ROI axis | methods \"planes were pooled for all analyses\" |\n| Select ROIs | `iscell[:,0]==1` | suite2p manual curation |\n| Per-trial masking | keep only samples `[trial_start-1 : teleport-1]`, everything else NaN | `preprocessing.dff(keep_teleports=False)` |\n| Neuropil subtraction | `F - 0.7*Fneu`, then add back the per-trial mean of `0.7*Fneu` | `preprocessing.dff` |\n| Baseline | per trial: `nansmooth(f,[0,15])` -> `minimum_filter1d(300)` -> `maximum_filter1d(300)` (~20 s at 15.5 Hz) | `preprocessing.dff`, methods |\n| dF/F | `(f - f0)/|f0|`, then `nansmooth(dff, 2)` per trial | `preprocessing.dff`, methods |\n| Deconvolution | `suite2p.extraction.dcnv.oasis(dff, 2000, tau=0.7, fs=frame_rate/n_planes)` per trial | `preprocessing.dff(deconvolve=True)`, methods |\n| Interneuron exclusion | drop cells with `corrcoef(dff, speed) > 0.5` over in-trial samples | `spatial.is_putative_interneuron` |\n| Final neural matrix | deconvolved \"events\", (n_neurons, n_timepoints) per trial, float32 | `glmUtils.get_timeseries_data` uses `sess.timeseries['events']` |\n\n### Temporal alignment / binning\n- **Alignment event**: start of the trial (`trial_start` frame, i.e. entry to the linear track at position 0 cm).\n- **Trial window**: `[trial_start-1, teleport-1)` frames (reference convention; excludes the teleport frame, whose\n  position value is interpolated across the teleport, and excludes the ITI).\n- **off_start = 0.0 s**, **off_end = None** (trials have variable length; mean 14.0 s).\n- **Time bin**: the native imaging frame period, 1/15.5078 Hz = **64.48 ms**, identical for every session\n  (2-plane sessions are sampled at 15.5078 Hz per plane). No re-binning: neural and behavior are already on the\n  same clock in the NWB file, which is exactly the sampling the paper used (\"All behavioral and neural time\n  series were sampled at ~15.5 Hz\").\n\n### Inputs (d_input = 4)\n| idx | name | type | source / transform |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | `time_from_trial_start` | time-varying, s | `timestamps - timestamps[trial_start-1]` |\n| 1 | `environment` | per-trial constant, broadcast in time | `environment` series: 0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2 (mode within the trial) |\n| 2 | `trial_number` | per-trial constant | index of the trial within the session (0-based, from `trial_start` order) |\n| 3 | `previous_trial_outcome` | per-trial constant | rewarded flag of trial i-1 (0 = omitted, 1 = rewarded); for the first trial of a session there is no previous trial -> set to 0 (\"not rewarded\"), documented below |\n\nAll inputs are stored as a (4, T) float32 array so every input is time-varying-compatible.\n\n### Outputs (d_output = 6)\n| idx | name | values | transform |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | `reward_zone_distance` | 7 bins | signed distance to the **nearest point of the reward zone**: `d = pos - zone_start` if `pos < zone_start`; `d = 0` if inside `[zone_start, zone_end]`; `d = pos - zone_end` if `pos > zone_end`. Bins: <-50; [-50,-10); [-10,0); ==0; (0,10]; (10,50]; >50 |\n| 1 | `position` | 5 bins | `pos` into 5 equal 90 cm bins of the 450 cm track |\n| 2 | `speed` | 5 bins | `speed` series: <2; [2,10); [10,20); [20,40); >=40 cm/s |\n| 3 | `lick` | 2 | `lick` cumulative count per frame > 0 -> 1 (methods: \"Remaining lick counts were converted to a binary vector\") |\n| 4 | `reward_zone_location` | 3 (A,B,C) | per-trial, from the scene name in `identifier` + the trial-30 switch rule (`behavior.get_reward_zones`); broadcast in time |\n| 5 | `reward_outcome` | 2 | per-trial `isreward` = (a reward was delivered inside the trial) AND (reward zone was entered), `behavior.get_trial_types`; broadcast in time |\n\nAll outputs are stored as a (6, T) int64 array (time-varying wherever possible, per Decoder Task instructions).\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Neural signal = deconvolved dF/F (\"events\"), recomputed with the reference pipeline**, not the NWB\n   `Deconvolved` series. Justification: the NWB `Deconvolved` is suite2p's `spks` computed on the raw F\n   (non-zero during the ITI, raw-F magnitude, r = 0.38 with the reference pipeline output), whereas the paper's\n   decoder/GLM explicitly use OASIS applied to the per-trial maximin dF/F. Reproducing `preprocessing.dff()`\n   keeps us consistent with the reference.\n2. **All 152 sessions included**, not just the 77 switch sessions. The decoder task's variables are defined on\n   every session, and more sessions give the decoder more data; the paper's restriction to switch days was\n   specific to its reward-relative remapping question.\n3. **No speed threshold.** The paper drops samples < 2 cm/s for spatial analyses, but (a) a decoder needs\n   contiguous, equally spaced time bins within a trial and (b) speed itself is a decoder output whose first bin is\n   defined as < 2 cm/s, so removing those samples would delete an entire output class. Documented deviation.\n4. **Trials with lick-sensor errors are dropped** (the paper NaNs their licks; we cannot store NaN in a\n   categorical output). Rule (from methods): > 30% of frames in the trial with cumulative lick count > 2.\n   This rule reproduces the paper's count of 81 trials exactly.\n5. **Teleport/ITI excluded** and the teleport frame itself excluded, matching `dff()` and\n   `glmUtils.get_timeseries_data`.\n6. **Previous-trial outcome for the first trial of a session = 0**. There is no preceding trial in the imaged\n   session (mice did run ~30 un-imaged warm-up trials beforehand, but those data are not in the file), so the\n   most conservative encoding is \"not rewarded\"; this affects 152 of 12,135 trials (1.3%).\n7. **Time bin = native frame period (64.48 ms)**, no re-binning, no smoothing beyond the reference's dF/F\n   smoothing.\n8. **Neuron curation** = `iscell` + interneuron exclusion (r(dF/F, speed) > 0.5), following methods.\n9. Sessions/trials with fewer than 2 trials would be dropped (none expected).\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [x] Number of sessions = 152, subjects = 11, switch sessions = 77 (paper: 77).\n- [x] Lick-error trials flagged = 81 (paper: 81).\n- [x] Reward-zone labels derived from the scene name match the positions where `reward_zone > 0` on every trial.\n- [x] Fraction of rewarded trials ~0.85 (paper: ~15% omission).\n- [ ] Trials/session mean ~80.5 +/- 7.4 (paper).\n- [ ] Neurons/session within 155-2172 (paper) after curation.\n- [ ] Interneurons excluded ~0.42 +/- 0.85% of cells (paper).\n- [ ] `reward_zone_distance == 3` (distance 0) occurs for exactly the samples with position inside the zone, and\n      the position bins of the zone match A/B/C.\n- [ ] Reward deliveries occur inside the reward zone on rewarded trials.\n- [ ] Output distributions: position roughly uniform across the 5 bins, speed mostly in bins 2-4.\n- [ ] Spot checks against raw NWB (Step 10): neural value at a given trial/neuron/time, position, speed, lick.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py` implements the plan of Step 5.
